authors: Turner GSC et al.
title: Evaluation of DGT as a long-term water quality monitoring tool in natural waters; uranium as a case study
water_body: River Enborne (Brimpton, Berkshire)
location_in_paper: SI Tables S5, S7a-c
notes: OLS of log10 C_DGT (U, Metsorb) on weekly-mean pH; rows used: weeks 1-21 excl. week 15 (no DGT); r = Pearson on log10 scale. U is an oxyanion-group element in this schema (uranyl-carbonate complexes) measured with Metsorb (TiO2). Very narrow pH range (<0.35 units) so slope is poorly constrained; pH co-varies with season, flow, alkalinity and (Enborne) DOC that rose from ~2 to ~9 mg/L in autumn runoff. Authors report no pH or DOC statistics for U; DGT/spot ratios scatter widely (0.27-2.05) partly from DBL and spot-sampling timing. Weekly-average dissolved U used for the dissolved slope to match the weekly pH average.

authors: Paller MH, Knox AS, Blas SA, Harmon SM
title: Use of Diffusive Gradients in Thin Films (DGT) to measure potentially bioavailable metals in southeastern USA blackwater streams
journal: Savannah River National Laboratory report SRNL-L3200-2021-00117 (field work Jun-Aug 2019)
water_body: Lower Three Runs, Steel Creek, Upper Three Runs (Savannah River Site)
location_in_paper: Table 1, Table 2
notes: OLS of log10(measure) on pH across 7 sites; pH assigned at STREAM level (3 distinct values: UTR 6.03, LTR 6.66, SC 6.80) so the slope is essentially UTR vs the other two streams and the 7 sites are pseudo-replicates. UTR also has lowest conductivity (22 vs 51-67 umhos/cm) and Ca; authors suggest DGT may over-measure in UTR because of low ionic strength. 5.5-d deployment, blackwater (DOC 3-4 mg/L). Authors state dissolved Cu and Pb were higher in UTR, possibly due to its lower pH. Filtered Zn (59-69 ug/L) and Cd (0.15-0.22 ug/L) are nearly uniform across all sites and far above DGT values, suggesting a filtration/contamination artefact; treat dissolved and fraction slopes for Zn/Cd with caution.

authors: Mueller KK, Lofts S, Fortin C, Campbell PGC
title: Trace metal speciation predictions in natural aquatic systems: incorporation of dissolved organic matter (DOM) spectroscopic quality
water_body: 8 lakes: Dasserat, Dufault, Opasatica, Vaudray (Rouyn-Noranda QC); Bethel, Geneva, Raft, Whitson (Sudbury ON)
location_in_paper: Table 1; text p. (Results) 'percentage of free metal tended to decrease as the pH increased'
notes: Not DGT: free ions by IET (Cd, Ni, Zn) or Cu-ISE (Cu). OLS of log10(measure) on field pH across lakes; excluded (NA/illegible): Bethel. Fraction computed as free/total from printed values (matches printed % to rounding). Authors: % free tended to decrease with increasing pH for all four metals in both regions (protons compete), and declined with DOC for Cd, Cu, Ni (statistics only in their SI, not seen). Confounders: two mining regions with very different total metal supply (Sudbury Ni, Rouyn-Noranda Cu/Zn), DOC 2-8 mg/L, Ca 68-464 uM; single summer survey. Fraction slope best isolates pH effect.

water_body: 8 lakes: Dasserat, Dufault, Opasatica, Vaudray (Rouyn-Noranda QC); Bethel, Geneva, Raft, Whitson (Sudbury ON)
location_in_paper: Table 1; text p. (Results) 'percentage of free metal tended to decrease as the pH increased'
notes: Not DGT: free ions by IET (Cd, Ni, Zn) or Cu-ISE (Cu). OLS of log10(measure) on field pH across lakes; excluded (NA/illegible): Dufault, Opasatica, Vaudray. Authors: % free tended to decrease with increasing pH for all four metals in both regions (protons compete), and declined with DOC for Cd, Cu, Ni (statistics only in their SI, not seen). Confounders: two mining regions with very different total metal supply (Sudbury Ni, Rouyn-Noranda Cu/Zn), DOC 2-8 mg/L, Ca 68-464 uM; single summer survey. Fraction slope best isolates pH effect.

authors: Priadi C et al.
title: Spatio-temporal variability of solid, total dissolved and labile metal: passive vs. discrete sampling evaluation in river metal monitoring
water_body: Seine downstream of Paris: Bougival and Triel (urban-impacted)
location_in_paper: Results text (Spearman correlation paragraph); Table 1 (pH, DOC ranges)
notes: n not stated: 13 monthly samples per site (Oct 2008-Oct 2009); Spearman correlation (printed as 'r2' but signed, so read as rho) between 0.45-um dissolved metal and pH at the downstream (anthropogenic) sites, analysed separately from upstream Marnay; text implies Bougival and Triel pooled (n up to 26) but n is not stated explicitly. Significant NEGATIVE correlation (higher dissolved metal at lower pH). Confounded: dissolved metals also correlated positively with DOC (Co 0.655, Cu 0.469, Mn 0.507, Ni 0.574) and temperature (Cd 0.531, Cu 0.523, Mn 0.602, Pb 0.724), i.e. a seasonal redox/organic signal (summer low flow, lower pH downstream of WWTP inputs). No correlations reported for DGT-labile metals or labile/dissolved ratios.

authors: Cleven R, Nur Y, Krystek P, Van den Berg G
title: Monitoring metal speciation in the rivers Meuse and Rhine using DGT
water_body: Rhine at Lobith; Meuse at Keizersveer
location_in_paper: Table II (period means: pH Rhine 8.03+/-0.62; Meuse 7.65+/-0.39 and 7.29+/-0.38); Fig. 6; text
notes: Deployments: Rhine n=11 (Feb-Jul 2003), Meuse n=12 (Feb-Jul) + 14 (Sep-Dec 2003). Labile fraction order Ni > Cu > Pb.
